subject.title: fix(cron): allow timeoutSeconds: 0 for no-timeout mode

question: Should the Control UI expose the existing cron `timeoutSeconds: 0` no-timeout sentinel, or keep the UI positive-only?
rationale: Backend and tool contracts already accept zero, but surfacing it to UI operators intentionally removes cron wall-clock timeout protection for those jobs, so automation should not decide that product/operational policy.

options.title: Expose no-timeout in UI
options.body: Accept the backend contract as the UI contract too, then require the branch to rebase, add tests, and provide real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Keep UI positive-only
options.body: Close this PR and keep `timeoutSeconds: 0` available only through lower-level API/tool paths until a separate UI policy decision changes that.

recommendation.title: Expose no-timeout in UI
recommendation.body: Accept the backend contract as the UI contract too, then require the branch to rebase, add tests, and provide real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They owned the cron UI edit-parity and advanced controls work that introduced the relevant form behavior.
